The graph, and how you find a person in it

Screens 1–6. Alex's third resort today is "ask a colleague, if one is reachable". This board makes reachability a designed property: a dual follow/connect model where each action's grants are stated, suggestions that always name their evidence, and an expert finder that answers a question rather than returning a ranked list of people.

2 FOLLOW vs CONNECT — THE DUAL MODEL, MADE LEGIBLE (C06) 1440 × 620 · one person card, two actions, every grant stated
PUBLIC PROFILE the two actions are never merged into one button, and neither is called "friend"

FOLLOW asymmetric · public · no permission needed
You start seeing their public activity. They are told once, and can do nothing about it — the same way you can read anyone's published papers without asking.
Grants you
their public artifacts in your feed · new method cards, null results, published papers, communities joined
Does not grant
Lab-visibility artifacts · direct messages · their contact details · anything private
Visible to
everyone · your following list is public, because who you learn from is part of your scientific record
Reversible in one click, silently. They are not notified when you unfollow.
CONNECT symmetric · they must accept · unlocks sharing
A request they accept or ignore. Accepting makes you mutually visible and opens the private channel — this is the edge that actually carries work between labs.
Grants both of you
direct messages without the reputation gate · the ability to share a Lab-visibility artifact one-to-one · warm-introduction paths through each other
Does not grant
access to your projects · your lab's data · anything your institution governs. A connection is a person-to-person edge, never an access-control decision.
Visible to
the two of you · connection lists are private by default, because they map collaborations that are not yet public
Either side can disconnect. The other is not notified, and any artifact already shared stays shared — revoking access is a separate, deliberate act on the artifact itself.
WHY TWO EDGES, NOT ONE
A single "connect" button forces every relationship into a negotiation. Most scientific attention is one-directional — you read someone's work for years without meeting them — and pretending otherwise produces the inbox of requests that makes existing networks unusable.
WARM INTRODUCTIONS · C17
Where you have no edge but a shared connection does, the profile offers Ask J. Krieger for an introduction — a request to your connection, never a message to the stranger. They forward it or they do not.
THE ONE THING THIS SCREEN MUST DO
Make the grant of each action legible before it is taken. Every access complaint on a social platform starts with a user who did not know what a button gave away.

3 FOLLOW NON-PERSON ENTITIES (C07) 700 × 620 · four kinds, four different notification shapes
FOLLOWING · NON-PERSON 32 of your 128 follows are not people
Most of what a researcher needs to keep up with is not a person. Each entity type produces a different kind of event, so each gets its own notification shape rather than one generic "new activity".
METHOD CARDMC-0288FOLLOWING
Tells you about: new versions, new failure modes, forks that diverge from yours, and a reproduction that contradicts it.
INSTRUMENT MODELBD FACSymphony A3FOLLOWING
Tells you about: newly reported failure modes, confirmed workarounds, firmware changes that invalidate old gates. Across every institution, not just yours.
DATASETDS-0904FOLLOWING
Tells you about: new versions, corrections, retraction of a linked paper, and anyone who reuses it. The reuse signal is the one people actually want.
PREPRINT SERVER · FILTEREDbioRxivFOLLOWING
Not the whole server — a saved query. Yours: crispr-knock-in AND (hek293t OR hek293), weekly digest.
≈ 6 papers / weekdigest, not per-item
Volume control is per entity type, not global — you can want every failure mode on your instrument and only a weekly digest from a preprint server. Set in notification controls.

EVIDENCE, NOT SELF-DESCRIPTION
The technique column shows what the person has actually produced — cards, datasets, accepted answers, logged sessions. Anyone can list cryo-EM in a bio; far fewer have seven method cards using it.
REACH IS SHOWN, NOT RANKED ON
Network distance is a column, never a sort key. The best person for the problem is frequently a stranger, and burying strangers is how a network becomes an old boys' club.

AI FOR RETRIEVAL, NOT AUTHORITY — APPLIED TO PEOPLE
The system does not say who is best. It says who has produced evidence of the technique, who has declared they are open to being asked, and how you can reach each of them. Ranking people by an inferred score is the single most damaging thing this product could do — it would make the platform an arbiter of scientific standing, and the field research was explicit that researchers do not want that.
WHAT IS ABSENT BY DESIGN
No match percentage on a person.
No "top expert" badge.
No ordering by h-index or seniority.
No contact without a stated route.
